newsitem.title: UK: MED OIL PRODUCTS FIRM AMID NAPHTHA, MOGAS GAINS.
newsitem.headline: MED OIL PRODUCTS FIRM AMID NAPHTHA, MOGAS GAINS.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly steady to slightly higher on Wednesday with prompt gasoline cargoes notionally $3 up and naphtha physical values seen $2 higher.
Tight prompt markets pushed first half August mogas up $3 but notional gains were more modest for the whole month.

NWE and Med cargo values were seen by dealers $2 up on the day after a naphtha physical trade at $196 CIF NWE for pipeline spec and a slight gain on August swap values confirmed firmer sentiments, despite lower crude futures values.
Gas oil was little changed but dealers said the tone was firmer in line with northwest Europe.
Premiums for Italian heating oil held around $3.50 to $4.00 a tonne above high quotes, perhaps 50 cents above recent levels.
"Its like the north, fairly tight in the prompt," said a trader who saw few prompt Russian cargoes on offer.
Cracked high sulphur fuel was still assessed strong, in the $83/$84 fob range. Two high density cargoes were still being offered by a French refiner but no buyers were seen.
High sulphur straight-run was steady but traders said that the arrival of fresh Iraqi crude on the Mediterranean market soon will make straight-run less attractive to refiners.

Traders said one Mersin stem of high sulphur straight-run was available from a European major. Two M-100 Russian cargoes will also be available soon at premia of $3 to $4 over high cif Med quote, the same level for two trades earlier this week.
One percent was unchanged with little activity reported in the market, but levels were notionally up following the stronger numbers in the north for low sulphur cargoes.
